newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Fed's Moskow sees scattered wage pressures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fed's Moskow sees scattered wage pressures.

text.p: The President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Michael Moskow said on Thursday he sees wage pressures in certain categories of employment in the United States.

Moskow, speaking to reporters at the Chicago Fed's Conference on Bank Structure and Competition, was asked about a key issue for Fed's policy at the moment -- whether tight labor markets are generating price pressures.

"The ECI (Employment Cost Index) numbers show that continuation of pattern ... with some acceleration on the wage side but on the benefits side, the rate of increase slowing down... That balances this out," Moskow said, stressing the question is whether this scenario will continue to unfold.
"We see some wages that are going up; computer programmers are one. They are in great demand in the economy," Moskow said, noting that wage rises are more significant in certain sectors.
"We would like to see wages go up as long as productivity is increasing at the same time," Moskow also stressed.

Asked about whether the strong dollar has an impact on the economy, in particular of the export-oriented Midwest, Moskow said "I hear anecdotes occasionally, people have mentioned the stronger dollar ... may encourage exports into the United States."

But Moskow also made the point that a recent study by the Chicago Fed has found that Midwest exports were particularly healthy to countries whose currencies actually fell against the dollar because U.S. products are highly competitive.
